condition: Nutritional Anemia in Adults & Reproductive Age
diagnostic_criteria: Hemoglobin < 12.0 g/dL in non-pregnant adult females
Grading under ICMR criteria: Mild (10.0-11.9 g/dL), Moderate (8.0-9.9 g/dL), Severe (< 8.0 g/dL)
Microcytic Hypochromic index: MCV < 80 fL and MCH < 27 pg
recommended_investigations: Complete Hemogram with automated red cell indices (MCV, MCH, RDW)
Peripheral blood smear examination for red cell morphology (microcytes, hypochromia, poikilocytosis)
Serum Ferritin (< 30 ng/mL diagnostic of iron deficiency in non-inflammatory state)
Stool examination for ova, cysts, and occult blood to exclude intestinal parasitic infestation or gastrointestinal blood loss
Urine examination for microscopic hematuria in recurrent or unexplained anemia
lifestyle_precautions: Increase dietary intake of iron-rich foods: green leafy vegetables, jaggery, germinated pulses, lentils, and animal source proteins where accepted
Co-ingest Vitamin C rich foods (amla, lemon, guava, citrus fruits) with meals to enhance elemental non-heme iron absorption
Avoid consuming tea, coffee, milk, or antacids within 1 hour before or after main meals due to tannin and polyphenol inhibition
Promote personal hygiene, handwashing, and footwear usage to prevent soil-transmitted hookworm re-infection

medicines.name: Ferrous Ascorbate / Ferrous Sulphate (Oral Elemental Iron)
medicines.notes: 100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg Folic Acid once daily on empty stomach or between meals. Continue for 3 to 6 months to replenish marrow iron stores after Hb normalization.

medicines.name: Folic Acid
medicines.notes: 5 mg daily orally, co-administered with iron therapy.

medicines.name: Albendazole
medicines.purpose: Mandatory deworming protocol per ICMR national guideline
medicines.notes: 400 mg single oral dose, chewable at bedtime. Repeat after 6 months in endemic regions. Contraindicated in first trimester of pregnancy.

medicines.name: Intravenous Iron Sucrose / Ferric Carboxymaltose
medicines.purpose: Parenteral therapy for severe anemia or oral intolerance
medicines.notes: Administer calculated Ganzoni dose under emergency institutional supervision for severe anemia in second/third trimester or oral non-compliance.

red_flags_refer_to_doctor: Severe anemia (Hemoglobin < 7.0 g/dL) with tachycardia, congestive heart failure signs, or dyspnea at rest
Anemia in pregnancy with gestational age > 34 weeks requiring urgent parenteral replenishment
Failure of Hemoglobin to rise by at least 1.0 g/dL after 3-4 weeks of compliant oral iron therapy
Suspected gastrointestinal bleed (melena, hematemesis, or hematochezia)
follow_up: Reticulocyte response assessment at 7-10 days following treatment initiation
Repeat Hemoglobin measurement at 4 weeks to verify therapeutic response (> 1 g/dL rise)
Continue maintenance iron therapy for 3 months after Hemoglobin reaches normal reference interval
Post-treatment counseling on sustaining iron-adequate nutritional intake
